author: vanaukenk
body:
* **PANTHER:PTN002263325 and PANTHER:PTN000159004**

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name): P49590, P12081 as well as mouse, rat, and Xenopus**

* **Type of Issue: It looks like human, mouse, rat, and Xenopus have two genes for Histidine--tRNA ligase that have specialized in localization of their gene products to cytosol or mitochondria, whereas zebrafish, invertebrates and yeast have a single gene whose products localize to both via alternative splicing.**

* Add the label 'high priority' if needed. Generally high priority issues affect a lot of proteins, and annotations are incorrect (as opposed to just imprecise).

See:  https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0185317
See: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28321488/

Thanks!
title: Check CC annotations to HARS1 and HARS2 for mammals and frogs

author: marcfeuermann
body:
Thanks for pointing this out. Indeed the CC annotations were not correct. I've also reviewed the BP annotations since mitochondrial translation was added to the cytosolic members but was removed from the mitochondrial members. Something weird happened here. I also could extend the MF and BP up to bacteria.
Cheers,
Marc
